subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Positional Goods
description: A short lesson to help you apply Positional Goods.

hook.text: Would you prefer $100K where peers earn $200K, or $50K where peers earn $25K? Most choose $50K.

buildup.text: Positional goods derive value from ranking, not absolute level. A bigger house matters only if neighbors have smaller.

discovery.text: Frank showed that positional competition drives overspending on housing, cars, and education.

twist.text: This is a zero-sum arms race. Every upgrade is canceled by others upgrading.

climax.text: Positional spending traps families in debt. Investing in non-positional goods like health and leisure yields more.

punchline.text: Running faster in a race where nobody moves ahead is just exhaustion.

quiz.question: What are positional goods?
options: Goods that are valuable based on absolute quality
Goods whose value depends on ranking relative to what others have
Goods that can only be purchased in limited positions
